# Composite author audit — production, 2026-09-12

**Generated by** `npx tsx scripts/audit-contributors.ts --names-file docs/seo/author-names.json --identity <identity.json> --json docs/seo/composite-authors-audit.json`

**Read-only.** Nothing in this report was written to any database, and no
identity below has been created, split, renamed or redirected.


## Where these names came from

Over **HTTP, from production** — the `/authors` hub publishes every contributor
as an `ItemList` in its own JSON-LD, so one request yields the full set. This
matters: `.env.local` on a developer machine points at a LOCAL Supabase stack,
so a database query here would not be evidence about production
(SEO 3.1 §43). The machine-readable companion is
`composite-authors-audit.json`; the raw input is `author-names.json`.

**Total contributor expressions: 156.** Role marker stored inside the name: **16**.


## What each category means for migration

- **`SAFE_SINGLE`** — already correct. No action.
- **`SAFE_MULTIPLE`** — the byline separates deterministically into several
  people. These are the rows a future migration *could* split, and every one of
  them carries the URL problem: `/authors/a-b-c` has **2–5** valid successors
  and therefore **no single 301 target**. That is a product decision, not a
  script (SEO 3.1 §6.3, §21).
- **`ORGANIZATION`** — a corporate body. Never split: its name legitimately
  contains the delimiters a list uses, so splitting fabricates entities.
- **`INSTITUTION`** — the library's own institution appearing as an author.
  Must resolve to the site graph's existing `#organization` node, never a
  `Person` and never a second organization node.
- **`AMBIGUOUS`** — names more than one entity but cannot be separated safely
  (an inverted single name is indistinguishable from a two-name list). Requires
  human review; **zero** of these exist in the current collection.

## `INSTITUTION` — the library's own identity, stored as an author

- `Phnom Penh Teacher Education College` — Matches the published institutional identity; must reference the existing #organization node, never a Person.
- `វិទ្យាស្ថានគរុកោសល្យរាជធានីភ្នំពេញ` — Matches the published institutional identity; must reference the existing #organization node, never a Person.

Both the English and the Khmer institutional names exist as **separate author
rows**, so the institution is duplicated inside the author table itself. Since
SEO 3.0 both render as an `@id` reference to `#organization` rather than a
`Person`, so the published entity graph is already correct; the duplication is
a data-layer fact awaiting the migration decision.

`resource_contributors.role` (migration 0105) has a column for this, with
`editor`, `translator` and `compiler` already in its CHECK. Ingestion now
records it there. The legacy `authors.name` still contains the marker, and
normalising those names is part of the deferred migration — it would change
the slug, and therefore the URL, of every row above.
